intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, and matcha treats from legendary local vendors. Engage with vendors who have operated stalls for generations and discover the true heart of Tokyo's food culture.

experiences.name: Akihabara Electric Town Tech Immersion
experiences.description: Dive deep into Tokyo's iconic tech and otaku district, exploring multi-floor electronics shops, retro game arcades, robot cafes, and cutting-edge gadget stores. Visit Yodobashi Camera and smaller indie shops to experience Japan's unparalleled consumer electronics culture firsthand.

experiences.name: TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Experience one of the world's most celebrated immersive digital art installations where technology and creativity merge. Walk through infinite light forests, interactive water worlds, and AI-driven art environments that respond to your presence, representing the pinnacle of Japan's tech-art fusion.

experiences.name: Ramen Alley Crawl in Shinjuku
experiences.description: Navigate the narrow, atmospheric lanes of Shinjuku's Omoide Yokocho and nearby ramen shops to taste regional ramen styles including tonkotsu, shoyu, and miso broths. Chat with local chefs, slurp noodles at tiny counter seats, and experience the authentic izakaya dining culture Tokyo is famous for.

experiences.name: Odaiba Futuristic Waterfront & Toyota Mega Web
experiences.description: Spend a day on Tokyo's artificial island exploring the futuristic architecture, the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (Miraikan), and the Toyota Mega Web showroom featuring concept cars and driving simulators. The waterfront offers stunning views of the Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo skyline.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Haneda or Narita Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, pick up a prepaid IC card (Suica or Pasmo) at the airport for cheap train travel. Take the airport express train to your hotel area. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Do a quick convenience store run at a nearby 7-Eleven or FamilyMart for late-night snacks and essentials.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Late-night convenience store meal (onigiri, instant ramen, sandwiches) — budget approx ¥500–¥800

day_by_day.notes: Grab a free city map at the airport tourist info desk. Download Google Maps offline for Tokyo. Exchange a small amount of cash as many budget spots are cash-only. Rest well — big days ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Recover from jet lag with a slow morning. Walk around your hotel neighborhood to get oriented. Find a local kissaten (old-school Japanese coffee shop) for a classic morning set — coffee plus toast and egg for under ¥600. Head to nearby Odaiba waterfront (if hotel is beachfront-adjacent) for a free morning walk with views of Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo Bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Yurikamome line or bus to Akihabara — Tokyo's legendary tech and electronics district. Browse multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera and Akihabara Radio Kaikan for the latest gadgets, retro tech, and components. Window-shop and explore the dense side streets filled with anime, manga, and tech culture. Entry to most shops is free.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara for dinner. Try a budget ramen shop or a standing sushi bar (kaitenzushi conveyor belt sushi) for an affordable and authentic meal. Explore the glowing neon streets of Akihabara at night — a quintessential Tokyo tech-culture experience.

meals.breakfast: Kissaten morning set (coffee + toast + egg) — ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Convenience store bento or cheap teishoku set meal near Akihabara — ¥600–¥900
meals.dinner: Kaitenzushi (conveyor belt sushi) in Akihabara — ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best explored on foot. Many shops open around 10–11am. Look for multi-floor maid cafes and retro game shops for free browsing. Keep receipts — some electronics stores offer tax-free shopping for tourists.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Tsukiji Outer Market (free entry) — the world-famous fish market area. Arrive by 8–9am for the freshest experience. Browse stalls selling fresh seafood, tamagoyaki (sweet egg omelette), and street snacks. This is a must for local food lovers. Try a fresh tuna sashimi breakfast bowl (kaisendon) from one of the market stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus to Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300 entry) — a stunning traditional Japanese garden with a tidal pond right in the middle of the city. Afterward, cross over to Shiodome and browse the free Panasonic Shiodome Museum or simply walk the futuristic Shiodome media district to soak in Tokyo's tech-meets-architecture vibe.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shimbashi for dinner — a neighborhood packed with izakayas (Japanese gastropubs) popular with Tokyo salarymen. Order yakitori skewers, edamame, and draft beer at a standing izakaya for a very local, very affordable experience. The smoky alleyways here are iconic Tokyo.

meals.breakfast: Fresh seafood bowl or tamagoyaki at Tsukiji Outer Market — ¥800–¥1,200
meals.lunch: Soba noodles at a local Shiodome noodle shop — ¥700–¥900
meals.dinner: Standing izakaya in Shimbashi — ¥1,200–¥1,800 including drinks

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is busiest and most vibrant in the early morning. Hamarikyu is especially beautiful in spring with cherry blossoms or spring flowers. Bring cash for market stalls.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Asakusa — Tokyo's most traditional neighborhood. Visit Senso-ji Temple (free entry) early morning before crowds arrive. Walk the Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional snacks like ningyo-yaki (small cakes) and ningyoyaki. Explore the back streets of Asakusa for artisan craft shops and old Tokyo atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Sumida River toward the Tokyo Skytree area. Skip the expensive observatory (¥2,100+) and instead enjoy free views from the base plaza and surrounding shopping complex Solamachi. Browse the tech and lifestyle shops inside Solamachi for free. Cross the river and explore the free Edo-Tokyo Museum exterior or nearby Ryogoku area (sumo district).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Asakusa for dinner. Try a tempura teishoku set at a local tempura restaurant or grab a budget yakitori dinner at a small local grill. Walk the illuminated Nakamise street and Senso-ji at night — magical and free.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast at a local Asakusa cafe or onigiri from convenience store — ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Ramen at a local Asakusa ramen shop — ¥800–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Tempura teishoku set meal in Asakusa — ¥900–¥1,300

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is most atmospheric at dawn or dusk with far fewer tourists. The Nakamise street snacks make excellent cheap souvenirs. Asakusa is very walkable — wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Shibuya. Start with the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing — watch the organized chaos from street level (free). Visit the Hachiko statue for a photo. Head up to the free Shibuya Sky observation deck alternative — the rooftop of Mag's Park (Shibuya 109-2 area) or simply enjoy free views from the Starbucks overlooking the crossing (buy a ¥500 drink for a window seat).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shibuya's tech and youth culture: browse Loft (lifestyle and stationery store), Tower Records (free browsing), and the many electronics and gadget shops along Shibuya's back streets. Head to nearby Daikanyama for a relaxed walk through one of Tokyo's trendiest low-key neighborhoods — the T-Site Tsutaya bookstore complex is free to browse and stunning.
day_by_day.evening: Walk from Daikanyama to Nakameguro along the Meguro River. This canal-lined neighborhood is perfect for an evening stroll. Grab a cheap bowl of gyudon (beef bowl) at Yoshinoya or Sukiya (¥400–¥500) before heading back, or try a local ramen shop in Nakameguro.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at a local Shibuya bakery — ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Yoshinoya gyudon beef bowl in Shibuya — ¥400–¥600
meals.dinner: Ramen or tsukemen dipping noodles in Nakameguro — ¥900–¥1,100

day_by_day.notes: Shibuya Scramble is most impressive during rush hour (8–9am or 5–7pm). Daikanyama is a short 10-minute walk from Shibuya. Nakameguro is especially beautiful in spring with cherry blossoms over the canal.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Harajuku. Walk through Takeshita Street (free) — Tokyo's wild youth fashion street packed with crepe shops, quirky clothing stores, and street food. Grab a famous Harajuku crepe for breakfast. Afterward, cross into the peaceful Meiji Jingu Shrine (free entry) — a forested Shinto shrine offering a complete contrast to the surrounding chaos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from Harajuku along Omotesando Boulevard — Tokyo's tree-lined luxury shopping avenue. Window-shop the flagship stores of major tech and design brands (Apple Store, etc.) for free. Cut into the backstreets of Ura-Harajuku (Cat Street) for independent boutiques and street food. Take the train to Shinjuku and explore the massive Yodobashi Camera electronics megastore (free browsing, 9 floors of tech).
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Shinjuku for dinner. Head to Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — a narrow alley packed with tiny yakitori stalls serving skewered chicken, offal, and cold beer. Extremely atmospheric and budget-friendly. Afterward, walk through the neon-lit streets of Kabukicho entertainment district for free night sightseeing.

meals.breakfast: Harajuku crepe (strawberry, Nutella, or matcha) — ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Cheap teishoku lunch set in Omotesando side street — ¥800–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Yakitori skewers and beer at Omoide Yokocho, Shinjuku — ¥1,200–¥1,800

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free but a ¥1,000 inner garden fee applies — skip it on a budget. Omoide Yokocho is cash-only. Shinjuku at night is one of Tokyo's most spectacular free experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic man-made island. Take the scenic Yurikamome automated driverless train (great views, use IC card). Visit the free teamLab Digital Art Museum exterior and the free Odaiba beach area. Walk the futuristic promenade with views of Rainbow Bridge and the miniature Statue of Liberty replica.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (free entry) — home to a massive life-size Unicorn Gundam statue (free, iconic tech-culture landmark). Browse the free floors of Aqua City Odaiba mall and the free Toyota Mega Web (Toyota's interactive car showroom and driving experience — free entry). Enjoy the futuristic architecture and bay views.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward central Tokyo. Stop in Ginza for a free evening walk through Japan's most upscale shopping district — window-shop the Apple Store, Sony Park (free interactive space), and the illuminated boulevards. Find a budget sushi conveyor belt restaurant (kaitenzushi) in the area for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast eaten on the Yurikamome train — ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Food court meal at DiverCity Tokyo or Aqua City — ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Kaitenzushi conveyor belt sushi in Ginza — ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: The full teamLab Borderless or Planets museums cost ¥3,200+ — skip on a budget. Toyota Mega Web is free and surprisingly fun for tech lovers. Sony Park in Ginza has free rotating tech and art installations.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Ueno. Start with Ueno Park (free entry) — a massive public park home to multiple museums and shrines. Visit the free Toshogu Shrine within the park. Browse the outdoor flea market stalls often found along the park paths on weekends. Head to Ameyoko Market — a lively open-air market street packed with cheap food stalls, fresh produce, and bargain goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Nature and Science in Ueno Park (¥630 entry — one of Tokyo's best budget museum deals with incredible tech and science exhibits). Alternatively, visit the Tokyo National Museum (¥1,000) for Japanese cultural artifacts. After museums, head to nearby Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods. Walk the Yanaka Ginza shotengai (shopping street) for cheap local snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Yanaka Cemetery at dusk (free, atmospheric, not spooky) and the surrounding temple streets. Head back toward Ueno or Nippori for a cheap donburi (rice bowl) dinner at a local family restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit and snacks from Ameyoko Market stalls — ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Cheap street food lunch in Ameyoko (takoyaki, yakitori, fresh seafood) — ¥600–¥900
meals.dinner: Donburi rice bowl at a local Ueno family restaurant — ¥700–¥1,000

day_by_day.notes: Ameyoko is busiest and most fun on weekends. Yanaka is one of the few Tokyo neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing and retains Edo-period street layouts. Great for photography.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Akihabara for a second, deeper visit. This time focus on the retro tech and gaming culture: visit Super Potato (vintage video game store across multiple floors), explore the component electronics shops in the Radio Kaikan building, and browse the free floors of the Akihabara UDX tech convention center. Look for the free tech demo events often held here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to nearby Kanda and Jimbocho — Tokyo's legendary used bookstore district. Browse hundreds of second-hand bookshops, vintage map stores, and print shops (many have English sections). This is a fascinating, free, and very local cultural experience. Walk to the nearby Kanda Myojin Shrine (free) — famously associated with IT and tech industries, many tech companies come here for blessings.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Akihabara or Kanda for dinner. Try a cheap curry rice (kare raisu) at a local CoCo Ichibanya curry chain or a nearby katsu curry shop. Explore the glowing Akihabara streets one more time at night.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast — ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Standing soba or udon noodles near Akihabara — ¥500–¥700
meals.dinner: Katsu curry at a local curry shop — ¥800–¥1,100

day_by_day.notes: Kanda Myojin Shrine sells unique IT-themed omamori (charms) — a quirky and affordable souvenir for tech lovers (¥500–¥1,000). Jimbocho is best explored slowly — budget extra time if you love books.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Shinjuku. Visit the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (free, opens 9:30am) — one of the best FREE panoramic views of Tokyo including Mt. Fuji on clear days. Arrive early to avoid queues. Spend the morning enjoying the view and the free lobby exhibits about Tokyo's urban planning and tech infrastructure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (¥500 entry) — a beautiful blend of Japanese, French, and English garden styles. Perfect for a relaxed afternoon picnic. Grab cheap bento from a nearby convenience store to eat in the garden. Afterward, explore the Shinjuku underground shopping malls (free browsing) and the massive Takashimaya Times Square department store.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's bohemian neighborhood known for vintage shops, live music venues, and indie food culture. Browse the free vintage clothing stores and record shops. Find a small local izakaya or standing bar for a cheap dinner and drinks in this very non-touristy, local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Bakery breakfast near Shinjuku station — ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Convenience store bento picnic in Shinjuku Gyoen — ¥500–¥800
meals.dinner: Izakaya dinner in Shimokitazawa — ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: The Metropolitan Government Building has two towers — both offer free observation. Check opening hours as one may close on certain days. Shimokitazawa is a 15-minute train ride from Shinjuku on the Odakyu or Keio Inokashira line.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kawagoe (Little Edo) — only 30–40 minutes from Shinjuku by train (¥470 one way). Walk the beautifully preserved Kurazukuri Street with its Edo-period warehouse-style buildings (free to walk). Visit the free bell tower and explore the narrow Candy Alley (Kashiya Yokocho) for traditional Japanese sweets and snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Kawagoe. Visit Kitain Temple (¥400 entry) — featuring 540 unique stone statues of Buddha's disciples. Explore the Kawagoe Hikawa Shrine (free) — famous for its wind chime tunnel and relationship charms. Browse the local sweet potato (imo) products that Kawagoe is famous for — try imo soft serve ice cream (¥300–¥400).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by train. Head to a local neighborhood near your hotel for a relaxed dinner. Try a local tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) restaurant or a budget teishoku set meal. Rest up for the remaining days.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast before departing — ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Local Kawagoe eel (unaju) or sweet potato dishes at a casual restaurant — ¥900–¥1,300
meals.dinner: Tonkatsu teishoku set near hotel — ¥900–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Kawagoe is best reached via the Tobu Tojo Line from Ikebukuro or Seibu Shinjuku Line. A day pass may be cost-effective if available. Kawagoe is a refreshing break from central Tokyo's intensity.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Ikebukuro — Tokyo's underrated tech and otaku district (often overshadowed by Akihabara). Visit Sunshine City complex — a massive mall with free floors, an aquarium (skip on budget), and the free Sunshine City observatory exterior. Browse Animate (massive anime merchandise store — free to browse) and the dense electronics and manga shops of the area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the free Ikebukuro underground shopping arcades and the Tokyu Hands lifestyle and gadget store (free browsing). Head to nearby Sugamo — known as 'Grandma's Harajuku' — a traditional old-fashioned shopping street with cheap local food stalls, herbal medicine shops, and a very local, non-touristy vibe. Visit Koganji Temple (free) along the street.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ikebukuro for a final tech-culture dinner experience. Try one of Ikebukuro's famous ramen shops — the area is known for its diverse ramen scene including rich tonkotsu and spicy miso varieties. Do a final souvenir shopping run at the 100-yen shop (Daiso or Seria) for budget gifts.

meals.breakfast: Cheap bakery or convenience store near hotel — ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Street food snacks along Sugamo Jizo-dori shopping street — ¥500–¥800
meals.dinner: Ikebukuro specialty ramen — ¥900–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Ikebukuro's Sunshine City is free to enter and worth exploring even without paid attractions. Sugamo is one of Tokyo's most authentic local neighborhood experiences — very few tourists. 100-yen shops are excellent for cheap, quality souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo. Wake up early for a last walk around your hotel's beachfront neighborhood. Grab a final Japanese breakfast at a local kissaten or convenience store. Do any last-minute packing and souvenir buying. If time allows, visit a nearby neighborhood shrine for a quiet farewell to the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage at the hotel or at a station coin locker (¥300–¥700). Take a final stroll through a nearby neighborhood. Head to the airport via train (Narita Express or Limousine Bus — ¥1,000–¥3,000 depending on airport). Allow at least 2–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Grab a final bento or ekiben (train station bento box) from the airport or station to enjoy on your journey — a delicious, affordable last taste of Japanese food culture.

meals.breakfast: Final kissaten morning set or convenience store breakfast — ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Airport or station ekiben bento box — ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: In-flight or airport meal

day_by_day.notes: Return your IC card (Suica/Pasmo) at the airport for a refund of remaining balance minus ¥220 handling fee — or keep it for a future Japan trip. Duty-free shops at Narita and Haneda are good for last-minute snack souvenirs (Kit Kat flavors, etc.). Confirm flight details the night before.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, and matcha treats from legendary local vendors. Engage with vendors who have operated stalls for generations and discover the true heart of Tokyo's food culture.

Visit Yodobashi Camera and smaller indie shops to experience Japan's unparalleled consumer electronics culture firsthand.

experiences.description: Experience one of the world's most celebrated immersive digital art installations where technology and creativity merge. Walk through infinite light forests, interactive water worlds, and AI-driven art environments that respond to your presence, representing the pinnacle of Japan's tech-art fusion.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - In transit (Flight UA arriving 22:30)
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Narita/Haneda Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and take the airport limousine bus or Narita Express to central Tokyo. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Grab a light convenience store snack from nearby 7-Eleven or FamilyMart to unwind.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane
meals.dinner: Late-night convenience store (konbini) snacks — onigiri, sandwiches, and hot drinks from 7-Eleven or Lawson near the hotel (budget-friendly, ~¥500–¥800)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is arrival only. Keep the evening completely free for transit and check-in. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance as arrival is late at 22:30. Purchase a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless train and bus travel throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Gentle recovery morning — sleep in and enjoy a slow start. Head to a local kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) near the hotel for a morning set (coffee + toast + egg). Explore the immediate neighborhood on foot to get your bearings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Ueno Park for a leisurely stroll. In mid-April, late cherry blossoms may still be visible. Explore Ueno's Ameyoko Market street for local snacks and souvenirs. Browse stalls selling dried goods, street food, and budget fashion.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Asakusa for your first proper Tokyo evening. Visit Senso-ji Temple illuminated at night, stroll Nakamise Shopping Street, and enjoy the atmospheric old-town vibe of Tokyo's most historic district.

meals.breakfast: Kissaten morning set near hotel — coffee, buttered toast, and boiled egg (~¥600–¥900)
meals.lunch: Ameyoko Market street food — yakitori skewers, takoyaki, and fresh fruit (~¥800–¥1,200)
meals.dinner: Asakusa ramen or tempura restaurant — try Asakusa Mugimaru for hearty ramen or Daikokuya for traditional tempura donburi (~¥1,200–¥1,800)

day_by_day.notes: Keep this day relaxed to recover from jet lag. Avoid overloading the schedule. Asakusa is very walkable and close to Ueno, making it ideal for a low-effort but rewarding first full day.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — Arrive at Tsukiji Outer Market by 8:00 AM to beat the crowds. Sample fresh sushi at a standing sushi bar, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled egg omelet) from Tsukuji Yamagishi, grilled seafood skewers, and fresh oysters. This is one of Tokyo's premier food experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Ginza for window shopping and people-watching along one of Asia's most glamorous boulevards. Visit the Itoya stationery flagship store (9 floors of beautiful Japanese stationery and design goods). Explore the Sony Park or Uniqlo flagship for a taste of Japanese retail culture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tsukiji area or head to nearby Shimbashi for an izakaya dinner experience — a quintessential Japanese pub-style dining with small plates, grilled skewers, and cold beer.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market food tour — fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled scallops, and tamago onigiri (~¥1,500–¥2,500 total grazing)
meals.lunch: Ginza lunch set at a mid-range Japanese restaurant — many offer affordable teishoku (set meals) at lunch (~¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Shimbashi izakaya — order yakitori, edamame, karaage, and cold Sapporo draft beer (~¥2,000–¥3,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is busiest on weekends — arrive early (7:30–8:00 AM) to get the freshest items and avoid long queues. The inner wholesale market has moved to Toyosu, but the outer market remains a world-class food destination. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Akihabara Electric Town Tech Immersion — Spend the morning exploring Tokyo's legendary electronics and otaku district. Start with Yodobashi Camera's massive multi-floor electronics superstore, then dive into retro game shops, anime figure stores, and maid cafés. Visit Radio Kaikan for niche tech components and collectibles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue Akihabara exploration — visit Super Potato for retro video games, browse Kotobukiya for high-end collectible figures, and check out the latest gadgets at Sofmap. Optionally visit the Akihabara UDX building's tech showcases or a maid café for a uniquely Tokyo cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Head to nearby Kanda or Ochanomizu for dinner. Explore the bookshop district of Jimbocho on foot before settling into a local restaurant for the evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café — coffee and a morning pastry (~¥500–¥800)
meals.lunch: Akihabara lunch — try a curry rice restaurant or ramen shop in the district, many offer excellent value lunch sets (~¥900–¥1,300)
meals.dinner: Kanda or Ochanomizu izakaya or Japanese curry house — try CoCo Ichibanya for customizable Japanese curry (~¥1,200–¥1,800)

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is at its most vibrant on weekends with street performers and cosplayers near the main crossing. Budget extra time if you plan to shop — it is easy to spend 4–5 hours here. Many shops open around 10:00–11:00 AM on Sundays.

day_by_day.morning: Visit TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum — Book tickets in advance online (essential, as it sells out weeks ahead). Arrive at opening time for the best experience. Spend 2–3 hours immersed in the boundary-dissolving digital art installations where technology and nature merge into stunning interactive environments.
day_by_day.afternoon: After TeamLab, explore the Odaiba waterfront area. Visit DiverCity Tokyo Plaza and see the life-size Gundam statue outside. Browse the futuristic mall and enjoy views of Rainbow Bridge and the Tokyo skyline across the bay.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Odaiba for a sunset dinner with bay views. The waterfront area has numerous restaurants ranging from ramen to teppanyaki. Watch the Rainbow Bridge light up at dusk from the waterfront promenade.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel — onigiri, yogurt, and coffee (~¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Odaiba food court or Aqua City mall restaurants — varied options including sushi conveyor belt (kaiten-zushi) at Sushi no Musashi (~¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Odaiba waterfront restaurant — try Tableaux or a mid-range teppanyaki restaurant with bay views (~¥2,500–¥4,000)

day_by_day.notes: TeamLab Borderless tickets must be booked online well in advance — check the official teamLab website. The experience is best enjoyed without rush. Wear comfortable, preferably dark-colored clothing as the installations are more immersive. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours inside.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Harajuku — Start at Meiji Jingu Shrine for a peaceful morning in the forested grounds. Experience the contrast between the serene shrine and the vibrant youth culture just outside. Walk through Yoyogi Park if cherry blossoms are still lingering.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll down Takeshita Street for quirky Harajuku fashion and crepes, then transition to the more upscale Omotesando Avenue. Browse concept stores, Japanese designer boutiques, and the architecturally stunning Prada and Dior buildings. Visit Omotesando Hills mall.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya for the iconic Shibuya Scramble Crossing experience. Visit the Shibuya Sky observation deck for panoramic night views of Tokyo. Explore the vibrant nightlife streets of Shibuya for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Harajuku café — try a Japanese fruit sandwich (fruit sando) from a local bakery near the station (~¥600–¥900)
meals.lunch: Omotesando — mid-range lunch at a Japanese café or try Afuri ramen for yuzu-flavored light ramen (~¥1,200–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Shibuya — visit Ichiran Ramen for the famous solo-booth tonkotsu ramen experience, or explore the restaurant floors of Shibuya Hikarie (~¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Shibuya Sky tickets can be booked online in advance for a small discount. The scramble crossing is most spectacular at night with neon lights. Meiji Shrine is free to enter — the inner garden (Gyoen) has a small fee. Takeshita Street gets very crowded on weekday afternoons.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko — Take the Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa for a scenic 2-hour journey to Nikko. Explore the UNESCO World Heritage Toshogu Shrine complex, a breathtaking collection of ornately decorated shrines and mausoleums set in cedar forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — visit Rinnoji Temple, Futarasan Shrine, and walk the atmospheric cedar-lined paths. If time allows, take a short bus ride to Kegon Falls, one of Japan's most spectacular waterfalls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by late afternoon/early evening (approximately 2-hour return journey). Have a relaxed dinner near the hotel or in Asakusa.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before departing (~¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Nikko local restaurant — try yuba (tofu skin) cuisine, a Nikko specialty, at a restaurant near the shrine complex (~¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Asakusa neighborhood restaurant — try monjayaki (Tokyo-style savory pancake) at a local restaurant (~¥1,500–¥2,000)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Tobu Nikko All Area Pass for cost-effective travel to and around Nikko. Start early (depart by 7:30–8:00 AM) to maximize time at the sites. Nikko involves significant walking and stair climbing — wear sturdy shoes. The Toshogu Shrine entry fee is approximately ¥1,300.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shinjuku — Start with a morning visit to Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden, one of Tokyo's most beautiful parks and a top cherry blossom spot (late blooms possible in mid-April). Enjoy a peaceful stroll through the Japanese, French, and English garden sections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore East Shinjuku — visit Kabukicho entertainment district during the day to see the famous Robot Restaurant area and Godzilla head atop Shinjuku Toho Cinema. Browse Isetan department store's basement food hall (depachika) for an incredible array of Japanese delicacies and sweets.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — a narrow alley of tiny yakitori stalls near Shinjuku Station West Exit. Squeeze into a tiny stall for grilled chicken skewers, smoky atmosphere, and cold beer in one of Tokyo's most atmospheric dining spots.

meals.breakfast: Shinjuku café or bakery near the garden — coffee and a croissant or Japanese pastry (~¥700–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Isetan depachika basement — assemble a beautiful bento box or buy premium onigiri and Japanese sweets (~¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — yakitori skewers, offal, and cold beer at a tiny atmospheric stall (~¥2,000–¥3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen has a small entry fee (¥500). Alcohol is not permitted in the garden. Omoide Yokocho stalls are small and cash-only — bring yen. The alley is most atmospheric after dark from around 7:00 PM. Shinjuku is one of Tokyo's busiest areas — keep belongings secure.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Planets (Toyosu) — a different and equally stunning teamLab installation focused on bodily immersion (you walk through water and light). Book tickets online in advance. The experience takes approximately 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Toyosu Market — the modern replacement for the Tsukiji wholesale market. Book a viewing spot in advance to watch the famous tuna auction (requires early morning reservation, but afternoon tours of the facility are available). Browse the market building's restaurants for fresh seafood.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Roppongi for the evening — visit Mori Art Museum (open late on Fridays) for contemporary art with stunning Tokyo Tower views from the 52nd floor observation deck. Explore Roppongi Hills complex.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or nearby café (~¥600–¥900)
meals.lunch: Toyosu Market restaurant floor — fresh sashimi don (rice bowl with raw fish) at one of the market's acclaimed seafood restaurants (~¥2,000–¥3,500)
meals.dinner: Roppongi mid-range restaurant — try a Japanese-French fusion bistro or a reliable izakaya in the Roppongi Hills complex (~¥2,500–¥4,000)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Planets is a different experience from Borderless — both are worth visiting. Bring a change of clothes or be prepared to roll up trousers as you walk through shallow water installations. Lockers and towels are provided. Mori Art Museum is open until 22:00 on Fridays.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved historic neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing. Stroll through Yanaka Cemetery (beautiful and peaceful, especially with late cherry blossoms), browse the old-fashioned shotengai (shopping street) of Yanaka Ginza, and visit artisan workshops and local galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Nezu Shrine — a lesser-known gem with hundreds of torii gates (similar to Kyoto's Fushimi Inari but far less crowded). The shrine is particularly beautiful in spring. Then walk through Nezu and Bunkyo neighborhoods to explore Tokyo's intellectual and literary heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Koenji or Shimokitazawa for a bohemian evening — these neighborhoods are beloved by locals for their vintage shops, live music venues, and independent restaurants. Experience a more authentic, non-touristy side of Tokyo.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka bakery or café — try a local specialty melon pan or coffee at a charming old-style café (~¥600–¥900)
meals.lunch: Yanaka Ginza street food — menchi katsu (breaded minced meat cutlet), croquettes, and local snacks from market stalls (~¥800–¥1,200)
meals.dinner: Shimokitazawa local restaurant — excellent value at independent restaurants; try a Thai or Indian restaurant (Shimokitazawa has great ethnic food) or a local izakaya (~¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka and Nezu are best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. The neighborhood has excellent photo opportunities and a rare glimpse into pre-modern Tokyo architecture. Shimokitazawa is about 30 minutes from Yanaka by train — take the Chiyoda Line to Yoyogi-Uehara, then transfer.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura — Take the JR Yokosuka Line from Shimbashi (approximately 1 hour). Visit the Great Buddha (Kotoku-in Daibutsu), a 13-meter bronze Buddha statue dating from 1252. Explore Hase-dera Temple with its beautiful hillside gardens and sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Kamakura — hike the Daibutsu Hiking Trail through bamboo groves and past smaller shrines, or visit Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine, Kamakura's most important shrine. Browse the charming Komachi-dori shopping street for local crafts and snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Have a relaxed dinner near the hotel — perhaps try a neighborhood soba restaurant for a traditional and comforting meal.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store or onigiri before departing Tokyo (~¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Kamakura — try shirasu (whitebait) rice bowl, a local specialty, at a restaurant near Hase Station (~¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Local soba restaurant near hotel — cold or hot soba with tempura set meal (~¥1,200–¥1,800)

day_by_day.notes: The JR Pass covers travel to Kamakura. Depart Tokyo by 8:00–8:30 AM to have a full day. Kamakura is hilly — wear comfortable walking shoes. The Daibutsu Hiking Trail takes approximately 1.5 hours and offers stunning views but can be muddy after rain. Kamakura is very popular on weekends — arrive early.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Kagurazaka — Tokyo's former geisha district with a strong French influence. Stroll the charming stone-paved Hyogo Yokocho alley, browse boutique shops, and visit local temples. The neighborhood has a wonderful blend of Japanese tradition and European café culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (Miraikan) on Odaiba — a world-class science and technology museum showcasing robotics, space exploration, AI, and future technologies. Perfect for tech culture enthusiasts. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening splurge — visit the Tokyo Skytree observation deck (634 meters, the world's tallest tower) for spectacular night views of the entire Tokyo metropolitan area. Book tickets online in advance. Enjoy a farewell dinner in the Skytree Town complex.

meals.breakfast: Kagurazaka French bakery — Tokyo has some of Japan's best French bakeries; enjoy a croissant and café au lait (~¥800–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Kagurazaka restaurant — try a French-Japanese fusion lunch set or a traditional kaiseki-style bento at a local restaurant (~¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Tokyo Skytree Town — mid-range Japanese restaurant in the Solamachi complex below the tower; try a sushi or tempura restaurant (~¥2,500–¥4,000)

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan features ASIMO robot demonstrations at scheduled times — check the daily schedule on arrival. Tokyo Skytree tickets should be booked online to avoid queues. The Tembo Deck (350m) is included in the standard ticket; the Tembo Galleria (450m) requires an additional fee. Skytree is best at night.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — Revisit a favorite neighborhood or explore any missed spots. Visit a local shotengai (covered shopping street) for last-minute souvenir shopping. Pick up Japanese food souvenirs (omiyage) such as wagashi sweets, matcha products, and regional snacks from a department store basement.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for checkout and luggage collection. Head to the airport via Narita Express or limousine bus (allow 90–120 minutes travel time depending on your flight). Do final duty-free shopping at the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tokyo. Reflect on 13 incredible days exploring the city's food culture, tech innovations, historic neighborhoods, and natural beauty.

meals.breakfast: Final Tokyo breakfast — splurge on a beautiful Japanese breakfast set (gohan, miso soup, grilled fish, pickles, and tamagoyaki) at a local restaurant (~¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.lunch: Airport lunch — Narita or Haneda airport has excellent ramen, sushi, and bento options at mid-range prices (~¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: Check flight departure time carefully and plan airport transfer accordingly — allow at least 3 hours before international departure. Narita Airport is 60–90 minutes from central Tokyo; Haneda is 30–45 minutes. Confirm hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for a final morning of exploration. Tax-free refunds can be processed at the airport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, and matcha treats from legendary local vendors. Engage with vendors who have operated stalls for generations and discover the true heart of Tokyo's food culture.

experiences.name: Akihabara Electric Town Tech Immersion
experiences.description: Dive deep into Tokyo's iconic tech and otaku district, exploring multi-floor electronics shops, retro game arcades, robot cafes, and cutting-edge gadget stores. Visit Yodobashi Camera and smaller indie shops to experience Japan's unparalleled consumer electronics culture firsthand.

experiences.name: TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Experience one of the world's most celebrated immersive digital art installations where technology and creativity merge. Walk through infinite light forests, interactive water worlds, and AI-driven art environments that respond to your presence, representing the pinnacle of Japan's tech-art fusion.

experiences.name: Ramen Alley Crawl in Shinjuku
experiences.description: Navigate the narrow, atmospheric lanes of Shinjuku's Omoide Yokocho and nearby ramen shops to taste regional ramen styles including tonkotsu, shoyu, and miso broths. Chat with local chefs, slurp noodles at tiny counter seats, and experience the authentic izakaya dining culture Tokyo is famous for.

experiences.name: Odaiba Futuristic Waterfront & Toyota Mega Web
experiences.description: Spend a day on Tokyo's artificial island exploring the futuristic architecture, the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (Miraikan), and the Toyota Mega Web showroom featuring concept cars and driving simulators. The waterfront offers stunning views of the Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo skyline.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – In transit (Flight UA arriving at 22:30)
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Haneda/Narita Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange private luxury transfer (pre-booked limousine or black car service) to Aegean Bliss Resort, Tokyo. Check in, freshen up, and unwind in your premium suite.

meals.breakfast: On board flight
meals.lunch: On board flight
meals.dinner: Light late-night room service at Aegean Bliss Resort – request a curated Japanese welcome platter with sake, onigiri, and seasonal pickles to ease into Tokyo cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport meet-and-greet service for seamless customs assistance. Confirm concierge has your itinerary ready for Day 2. Store valuables in the in-room safe. Jet lag tip: stay hydrated and aim for at least 6 hours of sleep before the full Day 2 schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Gentle orientation morning – enjoy a premium Japanese breakfast at the hotel, then take a leisurely stroll along the waterfront near the resort to acclimate to Tokyo's atmosphere. Visit a nearby konbini (convenience store) like Lawson or 7-Eleven for a curated snack tasting – a quintessential Tokyo tech-meets-food experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Odaiba Futuristic Waterfront & Toyota Mega Web. Explore the iconic Rainbow Bridge views, the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (Miraikan), and the Toyota Mega Web showcasing cutting-edge automotive technology and future mobility concepts. Ideal introduction to Tokyo's tech culture.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner with a panoramic Tokyo Bay view at a high-end Odaiba restaurant. Return to the resort for a relaxing evening at the spa.

meals.breakfast: Full Japanese breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – grilled fish, miso soup, tamagoyaki, rice, and seasonal tsukemono
meals.lunch: Odaiba's Aqua City or DiverCity mall – visit Tableaux or a premium ramen counter for a sit-down gourmet lunch
meals.dinner: Tempura Kondo (reserve in advance) or Odaiba's high-end seafood restaurant with Tokyo Bay views – omakase-style tempura or premium kaiseki

day_by_day.notes: Odaiba is easily accessible from the waterfront area via the Yurikamome monorail or water bus – the water bus from Hinode Pier offers a scenic premium experience. Purchase a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the hotel concierge for seamless transport throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour – Begin early (around 8:00 AM) to experience the market at its freshest and most vibrant. Sample premium fresh sushi, hand-rolled tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, uni (sea urchin), and wagyu beef nigiri. Engage with vendors and learn about Tokyo's culinary heritage with a private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Tsukiji, head to Ginza for a curated exploration of Tokyo's most luxurious shopping district. Visit Dover Street Market, flagship tech stores, and the iconic Itoya stationery tower. Explore the Ginza Six rooftop garden for city views.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive omakase sushi dinner in Ginza – one of the world's finest sushi experiences.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market itself – fresh uni, otoro sushi, tamagoyaki, and matcha from market stalls (this IS the morning activity and meal combined)
meals.lunch: Sushi Saito (if reservation secured) or Sushi Yoshitake in Ginza – world-class nigiri omakase lunch course
meals.dinner: Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten or Sushi Sho – legendary omakase sushi dinner (reservations essential, book 2–3 months in advance via hotel concierge)

day_by_day.notes: The Tsukiji Outer Market tour should be booked with a private luxury food guide for the premium experience. Wear comfortable shoes – the market involves significant walking on uneven surfaces. Ginza is a 10-minute taxi ride from Tsukiji.

day_by_day.morning: Akihabara Electric Town Tech Immersion – Dive into Tokyo's legendary electronics and otaku district. Explore multi-floor electronics megastores like Yodobashi Camera and Bic Camera. Visit retro gaming floors, anime merchandise shops, and cutting-edge gadget stores. Consider a private tech guide to unlock hidden floors and insider spots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Akihabara – visit the Akihabara Radio Kaikan for rare tech collectibles, then head to the @cosme flagship store for beauty tech. Transition to nearby Ueno for a visit to the Tokyo National Museum to balance tech with cultural depth.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shinjuku for the Ramen Alley Crawl – navigate the atmospheric Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) and nearby premium ramen shops, tasting multiple styles including tonkotsu, shoyu, and shio ramen in the neon-lit alleyways.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a premium kissaten (Japanese coffee shop) near Akihabara – Chatei Hatou or a specialty third-wave coffee spot with artisan toast and eggs
meals.lunch: Akihabara maid café experience (premium tier) or a high-end Japanese curry house like Go!Go!Curry for an authentic local experience
meals.dinner: Ramen Alley Crawl in Shinjuku – Ichiran Ramen (private booth experience) followed by craft sake at a Shinjuku standing bar, then dessert at a premium wagashi (Japanese confectionery) shop

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is busiest on weekends – arrive by 10:00 AM to beat crowds. The Ramen Alley Crawl is best experienced after 19:00 when the neon lights fully illuminate the lanes. Book a private ramen guide for insider access to off-menu items and hidden shops.

day_by_day.morning: TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum – Experience the world-renowned immersive digital art installation where technology and art dissolve boundaries. Arrive at opening time (10:00 AM) for the most serene experience. Wander through infinite mirror rooms, living flower installations, and interactive light forests. This is a pinnacle of Tokyo's tech-art fusion culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: After TeamLab, explore the surrounding Azabudai Hills or Minato area – visit the newly developed Azabudai Hills complex, one of Tokyo's most futuristic urban developments, featuring luxury retail, art galleries, and innovative architecture by Heatherwick Studio.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar in Roppongi Hills (Tokyo City View observation deck or the Mori Art Museum rooftop), followed by a refined dinner in Roppongi.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – request a bento-style premium Japanese breakfast for an authentic touch
meals.lunch: TeamLab's in-house café or a nearby premium café in the Azabudai Hills complex – artisan sandwiches, seasonal salads, and specialty coffee
meals.dinner: Ryugin (3 Michelin stars) in Roppongi – a transcendent kaiseki experience blending traditional Japanese cuisine with avant-garde techniques, perfectly echoing the day's tech-art theme

day_by_day.notes: TeamLab Borderless tickets must be pre-booked online weeks in advance – the hotel concierge should secure these before the trip. Wear comfortable, dark-colored clothing for the best visual experience inside TeamLab. The Mori Art Museum rooftop offers one of Tokyo's finest panoramic views.

day_by_day.morning: Harajuku and Omotesando exploration – Begin with a peaceful morning walk through Yoyogi Park (cherry blossoms may still be visible in mid-April). Visit Meiji Shrine for a serene cultural experience. Then stroll down Omotesando, Tokyo's most architecturally distinguished boulevard, admiring flagship stores by Tadao Ando, Herzog & de Meuron, and other world-class architects.
day_by_day.afternoon: Deep dive into Omotesando luxury retail – visit the Prada Aoyama building, Louis Vuitton Omotesando, and the Nezu Museum with its exquisite Japanese art collection and bamboo garden. Explore the hidden Omotesando Hills complex for premium Japanese design brands.
day_by_day.evening: Shibuya crossing experience at night – witness the world's busiest pedestrian scramble from the premium Shibuya Sky observation deck, then transition to a private sake tasting experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Café Kitsuné in Omotesando – elegant pastries, specialty coffee, and a chic Parisian-Japanese ambiance
meals.lunch: Florilège (2 Michelin stars) in Aoyama – innovative French-Japanese cuisine in an open-kitchen setting, one of Tokyo's most exciting culinary experiences
meals.dinner: Narisawa (2 Michelin stars) – 'Innovative Satoyama Cuisine' blending Japanese nature philosophy with cutting-edge culinary techniques; a globally celebrated dining experience

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Shrine is best visited early morning (before 9:00 AM) for a tranquil atmosphere. The Nezu Museum garden is particularly beautiful in April with seasonal blooms. Book Shibuya Sky observation deck tickets in advance for the sunset time slot (around 18:00–18:30).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko or Hakone – choose based on preference. Recommended: Hakone for a luxury ryokan day experience. Depart early via the Romancecar (Odakyu luxury train) from Shinjuku. Arrive in Hakone, visit the Hakone Open Air Museum featuring outdoor sculptures and tech-art installations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hakone exploration continues – take the ropeway over volcanic Owakudani for dramatic views of Mt. Fuji (weather permitting in April). Visit Lake Ashi for a scenic cruise. Enjoy the hot spring (onsen) culture at a premium day-use facility.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo via the Romancecar, enjoying dinner on board or at a premium restaurant near Shinjuku upon return.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure – light and energizing
meals.lunch: Premium kaiseki bento or soba lunch at a Hakone ryokan restaurant – seasonal mountain vegetables, fresh tofu, and regional specialties
meals.dinner: Shinjuku Kappo Nakamura or a premium izakaya in Shinjuku upon return – wagyu beef, premium sake, and seasonal small plates

day_by_day.notes: The Romancecar observation car seats offer the best Mt. Fuji views – book in advance through the hotel concierge. April weather in Hakone can be misty, but this adds to the mystical atmosphere. Bring a small daypack with essentials as you'll be away from the hotel all day.

day_by_day.morning: Yanaka and Nezu neighborhood exploration – Tokyo's most beautifully preserved historic shitamachi (old town) district. Wander through the Yanaka Cemetery (famous for cherry trees), browse artisan craft shops, and visit the Yanaka Ginza shotengai (traditional shopping street) for a glimpse of old Edo culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Kagurazaka district – Tokyo's former geisha quarter with French-Japanese cultural fusion. Explore the hidden alleys (yokocho), visit the Bishamonten Zenkokuji Temple, and browse independent boutiques and galleries. This neighborhood perfectly blends tradition with modern Tokyo sophistication.
day_by_day.evening: Premium whisky bar experience at Bar High Five in Ginza or the Star Bar Ginza – world-class Japanese whisky and cocktail craftsmanship by master bartenders.

meals.breakfast: In-room premium breakfast at the resort – fresh fruit, artisan bread, Japanese-style eggs, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Kagurazaka's French-Japanese bistro – Brasserie Viron or a neighborhood kappo restaurant with seasonal kaiseki lunch set
meals.dinner: Kagurazaka Ishikawa (3 Michelin stars) – one of Tokyo's most revered kaiseki restaurants, celebrated for its exquisite seasonal ingredients and refined atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored on foot – wear comfortable walking shoes. The neighborhood has a relaxed, unhurried pace that provides a welcome contrast to Tokyo's busier districts. The whisky bar reservations should be made in advance as seating is extremely limited.

day_by_day.morning: Shibuya and Daikanyama tech-meets-lifestyle exploration – Begin at Shibuya's Scramble Square for panoramic city views, then explore the Shibuya Stream and Shibuya Cast complexes showcasing Tokyo's urban innovation. Visit the Google Japan office area (exterior) and the innovative Shibuya QS building.
day_by_day.afternoon: Daikanyama T-Site (Tsutaya Books) – one of the world's most beautifully designed bookstores and cultural hubs, beloved by Tokyo's creative elite. Browse curated books, vinyl records, premium stationery, and artisan goods. Continue to neighboring Nakameguro for a canal-side stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Nakameguro canal evening walk – one of Tokyo's most romantic and photogenic spots, lined with boutique restaurants and bars. Enjoy a premium dinner along the canal.

meals.breakfast: Saturdays NYC Café in Daikanyama or Log Road Daikanyama – specialty coffee and premium avocado toast or Japanese-inspired brunch
meals.lunch: Ivy Place in Daikanyama (within the T-Site complex) – elegant all-day dining with a seasonal menu in a lush garden setting
meals.dinner: Nakameguro canal-side restaurant – Onigiri Bongo (premium version) or Sushi Saito annex, or a reservation at a Nakameguro French-Japanese fusion restaurant with canal views

day_by_day.notes: Daikanyama T-Site is open until 26:00 (2:00 AM) – a unique Tokyo experience worth noting for night owls. The Nakameguro canal is particularly atmospheric in the evening with illuminated restaurants reflecting on the water. April may still have some late cherry blossom petals along the canal.

day_by_day.morning: Shinjuku deep dive – Morning visit to the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building's free observation deck for panoramic city views. Explore the Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden, one of Japan's finest – particularly beautiful in mid-to-late April with late-blooming cherry varieties and tulip gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore East Shinjuku's Kabukicho entertainment district (by day it's fascinating architecture and street culture). Visit the new Toho Cinemas Shinjuku building with its iconic Godzilla head. Then explore the Golden Gai district – over 200 tiny bars in six narrow alleys, a unique Tokyo institution.
day_by_day.evening: Premium experience: Book a private table at a Golden Gai bar for an intimate evening, or head to the Park Hyatt Tokyo's New York Bar (made famous by Lost in Translation) for jazz, cocktails, and Tokyo skyline views.

meals.breakfast: Shinjuku high-rise hotel breakfast or Isetan department store's basement food hall (depachika) – premium pastries, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Takashimaya Times Square's premium restaurant floor – soba at a renowned buckwheat specialist or a wagyu beef lunch
meals.dinner: Kozue at the Park Hyatt Tokyo (40th floor) – refined Japanese cuisine with sweeping city views, one of Shinjuku's most celebrated dining experiences

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen requires a small entrance fee and has rules about alcohol and drones. The Golden Gai bars are tiny (some seat only 5–6 people) – arrive early or have the concierge make reservations at one of the more upscale Golden Gai establishments. The Park Hyatt New York Bar has a cover charge after 20:00.

day_by_day.morning: Asakusa cultural immersion – Visit Senso-ji Temple at dawn (before 8:00 AM) for a serene, crowd-free experience. Watch monks perform morning rituals, explore the Nakamise shopping street for premium Japanese souvenirs (lacquerware, folding fans, tenugui textiles), and visit the Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center's rooftop for views of the Skytree.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tokyo Skytree – ascend to the Tembo Deck (350m) and Tembo Galleria (450m) for the highest views in Tokyo. The surrounding Solamachi complex offers premium shopping and Japanese craft goods. Visit the Sumida Aquarium on the lower floors for a tranquil interlude.
day_by_day.evening: Sumida River dinner cruise – a premium private or small-group boat experience gliding past illuminated bridges and the Skytree, with a curated kaiseki or French-Japanese dinner served on board.

meals.breakfast: Asakusa's historic Kamiya Bar (Japan's oldest Western-style bar, opens at 11:00) – or a traditional Japanese breakfast at a nearby machiya café
meals.lunch: Sometaro (traditional okonomiyaki) in Asakusa or a premium unagi (eel) restaurant like Nodaiwa Honten – unaju (eel over rice) is a Tokyo specialty
meals.dinner: Private Sumida River dinner cruise with kaiseki catering – arrange through the hotel concierge for a bespoke experience with sake pairing

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter and open 24 hours, but the inner hall has specific hours. Saturday mornings in Asakusa can get busy by 10:00 AM – early arrival is essential. The Skytree tickets should be pre-purchased online to skip queues. The river cruise is best booked 2–3 weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury leisure morning – Sleep in and enjoy a premium spa treatment at Aegean Bliss Resort (facial, traditional Japanese shiatsu massage, or onsen soak). This is a restorative morning before the final full day of exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Marunouchi and Imperial Palace East Gardens – Stroll through the elegant Marunouchi business district, visiting the premium Kitte building (a converted post office with a stunning atrium and rooftop garden overlooking Tokyo Station). Walk through the Imperial Palace East Gardens for a serene nature experience in the heart of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell premium shopping at Ginza – visit Ginza Six's rooftop garden, Mikimoto Pearl flagship, and the Hermès Maison Ginza building. End the evening with a celebratory dinner at one of Tokyo's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely in-room breakfast or hotel restaurant – champagne breakfast with seasonal Japanese and Western options
meals.lunch: Kitte Marunouchi's restaurant floor – premium ramen at Fuunji or a refined Japanese lunch set at one of the building's curated restaurants
meals.dinner: Joel Robuchon Tokyo (3 Michelin stars) in Ebisu or Quintessence (3 Michelin stars) in Shirokanedai – a world-class French-Japanese farewell dinner with exceptional wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Imperial Palace East Gardens are closed on Mondays and Fridays – Sunday timing is perfect.
